Both models accurately read the text and produced fluent audio. The core difference lies in their interpretation and execution of 'a shouting manner'.

Model 1 (T1) delivered the line with increased volume and an urgent tone, but it fell short of a true shout. It sounded more like a very loud, emphatic statement. The vocal quality was relatively clean, lacking the strain or 'edge' that typically accompanies shouting. 

Model 2 (T2) provided a significantly better rendition of shouting. The volume was higher, and more importantly, it incorporated a sense of vocal strain throughout the utterance, especially on the word 'Help!'. This added layer of vocal effort makes its performance much more convincing and aligned with the user's prompt. The difference is significant because T2's audio immediately evokes the image of someone shouting, whereas T1's audio requires more interpretation and is less direct in its compliance. Therefore, T2 demonstrates superior quality in controlling the 'Volume' feature to match the 'shouting' requirement.
